checks.finding: requirements.md REQ-002's amended snapshot-generation-mismatch row (ruling C(1), 2026-08-26) places its new mid-pipeline detection site 'immediately after step 5's validate-capability-registry and step 6's generate-registry-digest --whole dependency invocations complete.' REQ-001's own processing procedure is enumerated only as lettered steps (0),(a)-(m), never with an explicit numeric index anywhere in requirements.md itself; under the one numbering a reader can construct by counting that lettered sequence in order (0=1,a=2,...), step 5 corresponds to letter (d) (resolve-component-paths, which never touches the Registry), and letter (e) (discover and validate the Registry and compute registry_digest --whole) is a single combined step, landing at step 6, not split across two numbered steps 5 and 6. Downstream: a future author resolving where exactly to bind this new fail-closed TOCTOU-closing recheck has no single, self-consistent numbered-step index in the reviewed documents to anchor to, and the most literal reading of REQ-001's own lettered list produces an incorrect placement. Must be resolved before a design reviewer can safely fix the check's exact insertion point.

No direct conflict was found between requirements.md's goals, acceptance criteria, constraints, or non-goals (including the two 2026-08-26 amendment rows) beyond the step-reference imprecision captured under AMBIGUITY, which does not rise to a direct contradiction.

Both 2026-08-26 amendment sub-triggers (the C(1) mid-pipeline Registry recheck on snapshot-generation-mismatch, and the C(2) absent-component sub-trigger on dependency-output-malformed) have no corresponding acceptance-test obligation in the byte-unchanged acceptance-tests.md: AC-010/TEST-010 is satisfiable per-diagnostic-id without exercising either new condition (the enum stays sixteen, so existing per-id fixtures suffice literally), and the existing snapshot-generation-mismatch fixtures (AC-040/TEST-040, AC-048/TEST-048) cover only the pre-existing pre-publication recheck window (steps (l)/(m)), not the new mid-pipeline site; no AC/TEST row names the absent-component dependency-output-malformed sub-case. A future test author can satisfy every stated acceptance criterion while never exercising either newly-approved fail-closed behavior. Per the calibration's Amendment Re-Review Context, this defect stands on its own and is not suppressed by the amendment declaration.
requirements.md's Assumptions section (three items) each states its own resolution path or explicit fallback; none is disturbed by the 2026-08-26 amendment.

The package's irreversible-change boundary (journaled Prepare/Journal/Commit/Post-publication-verification/Complete publication transaction with journal-based rollback) is concretely testable via AC-038/AC-039/AC-047/AC-048/AC-049; the human-copy application boundary for the protected Resolver script path and any SKILL.md edit is explicit and testable (AC-026, AC-032); the A(1)/B(1) amendment records in investigation.md meet the calibration's evidence bar (full commit hashes, per-document SHA-256s, verbatim dated approval quotation).

Apart from the scoped step-reference ambiguity (AMBIGUITY) and the missing acceptance-test coverage for the two new sub-triggers (EDGE-CASE-COVERAGE), the package's Dependencies/Field Definitions/Design-Decision citations and its Acceptance Criteria table leave no other observed gap that would force a downstream design reviewer to invent product behavior.
